title: Steadfastness in Obedience and Salah Despite Friends’ Mockery
summary: If your child’s friends mock his commitment to Salah, remind him of the hadith of the Prophet ﷺ: «Seven whom Allah will shade in His shade on the Day when there is no shade except His shade»—among them, «a youth who grew up in the worship of his Lord» (Sahih al-Bukhari 660). The hadith praises growing up in worship in general, and his steadfastness in it during the age of ridicule is a great virtue for which he will be rewarded; there is no place for shame. Connect the hadith to his reality so he feels that his commitment is something to be valued, not mocked. Read with him the verses of Surah al-Mutaffifin (verses 29-34) together with their tafsir; they describe how the criminals mocked the believers in this world, then Allah’s words: ﴿فَالْيَوْمَ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا مِنَ الْكُفَّارِ يَضْحَكُونَ﴾ (Al-Mutaffifin: 34; interpretation of the meaning: “So Today those who believed are laughing at the disbelievers”)—meaning on the Day of Judgment, as Ibn Kathir explains in his tafsir. Make clear to him that these verses were revealed about the mocking disbelievers, so we do not apply them to his friends or call them disbelievers. The goal is not gloating but to reinforce his conviction that the laughter of others today does not measure the correctness of his stance. Follow up with him through teaching, example, and firmness with rifq (gentleness). If your child faces mockery from his friends for his Salah, this is an expected test, not an exception. Your role is to connect his commitment to obedience to Allah and His Messenger ﷺ and to follow up with him with firmness and rifq (gentleness), not blame at the first sign of social pressure. If the mockery repeats and becomes ongoing harm, seek support from the school or an adult you trust.
try_this: Today: Read with your child the hadith of the «seven whom Allah will shade» (Sahih al-Bukhari 660), and discuss together how he can respond with confidence, not defensiveness, if someone mocks him for his Salah.
reflection_prompts: Does your child know that the Prophetic hadith praises the youth who grew up in the worship of his Lord, and that his steadfastness despite mockery is part of that upbringing?
Do you follow up with him with firmness and rifq, or do you merely give the command without follow-up at the first sign of pressure?
